subject.title: fix: inject only shared auth into macos dashboard

question: Should macOS Dashboard browser auth exclude native device tokens and inject only configured shared gateway tokens/passwords, even if that removes automatic browser auth for users relying on stored operator tokens?
rationale: The linked issue and Dashboard docs support a shared-secret browser boundary, but a sibling open PR asks for native/operator token parity on the same surface, and the choice changes existing user authentication behavior.

options.title: Adopt shared-token-only browser auth
options.body: Proceed with this direction after rebasing it over current main and proving shared-token injection plus stored native-token exclusion on macOS.

options.title: Keep native/operator token parity
options.body: Close or replace this PR and continue with the sibling parity direction so the embedded Dashboard can use the same resolved native token as native clients.

options.title: Split by explicit mode
options.body: Require a design follow-up that preserves the compatible default and adds an explicit strict browser-auth mode only if maintainers want both behaviors.

recommendation.title: Adopt shared-token-only browser auth
recommendation.body: Proceed with this direction after rebasing it over current main and proving shared-token injection plus stored native-token exclusion on macOS.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the most recent Dashboard auth/reload work and introduced the native Dashboard surface affected by this policy choice.
